confirmed.title: Regression from the round-5 DSN nit fix: a Go DSN password with a ':' in it is shown in clear, though 4a284f9 masked it
confirmed.evidence:
**Cause.** DSN_USERINFO's password class changed from `[^\s@/]` at 4a284f9 to `[^\s/:]` at 4ed6449. This came from the round-5 nit, which was a W28=B perf item.
- When a password holds a ':', the match from the user fails.
- The scan then restarts after the ':' and masks only the tail, or nothing.

**probe-r6, neutral field `note`** (columns 7193877 / 4a284f9 / 4ed6449):
- `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:x9@tcp(db:3306)/app`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR. Head shows `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:[secret 2a68a01a]@tcp(db:3306)/app`.
- `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:@tcp(db)/app`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR, shown whole.
- `connecting with root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:x@tcp(10.0.0.5:3306)/orders?parseTime=true`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR.
- `app:Zq9SeCr3tVal:k@unix(/tmp/mysql.sock)/db`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR.
- `root:pa:Zq9…@tcp(…)`: head shows the `pa:` part.

**Fuzz.** fuzz-mask seed 11 (pct), 4a284f9 vs head, found 1 regression in 150K cases, of this class: `a%22:Zq9SeCr3tValroot:@tcp(h)` is masked at 4a284f9 and in clear at head. Against 7193877 there are 0 (it had no DSN rule).

**Docs.** README L419 now lists 'a DSN password with a `:` in it' under misses, so the change is documented. But under W28=B, cost is document-only, so trading masking for speed is the wrong direction. This is a regression of something previously masked, and a secret shown in clear (Data panel only; C=c holds).

votes.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. I reproduced it on a fresh clone at pr35 = 4ed6449. `git diff --name-status 561bd84..HEAD` lists only #35's own files: CHANGELOG.md, README.md, lib/data-diff.mjs, package.json and test/data-diff.test.mjs.

**Cause.** `git diff 4a284f9..HEAD` shows that DSN_USERINFO's password class changed from `[^\s@/]` to `[^\s/:]` (lib/data-diff.mjs:388). The comment at :379-380 now says "never across a ':'". This follows the round-5 nit's own suggestion to keep ':' out of the class (review-35e findings.json: "nit (W28=B: document)"). The author combined it with the low finding's "let the password reach the last '@'".

**Probe** (my own `probe.mjs`): neutral field `note`, checked through `sanitizeSnapshot` at 7193877, 4a284f9, head and a fix copy.
- `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:x9@tcp(db:3306)/app`: clear / masked / head `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:[secret a7f231ad]@tcp(…)` / masked.
- `root:Zq9SeCr3tVal:@tcp(db)/app`: head shows it whole.
- The `connecting with …@tcp(10.0.0.5:3306)/orders?parseTime=true` shape and `app:…:k@unix(/tmp/mysql.sock)/db`: head shows the secret.
- `root:pa:Zq9…@tcp`: head shows `pa:`, which is part of the password.
- `root:x9:Zq9SeCr3tVal:y@tcp`: head shows the secret.
- The same string as JSON under a neutral key (`{"conn":…}`): head shows the secret.
- `a%22:Zq9SeCr3tValroot:@tcp(h)`: masked at 4a284f9, clear at head, as the claim's fuzz case says.
- Only a secret-named field (`dsn`) is still masked whole.

**This is a real-world shape.** go-sql-driver/mysql's ParseDSN splits the userinfo at the first ':' and the last '@', and its README says passwords need no escaping. So `user:pa:ss@tcp(…)` is a valid DSN, and its password is `pa:ss`. The proposed fix reads it exactly that way: user up to the first ':', password up to the last '@'.

**Differential fuzz** (mine; a pass where version A shows the secret in clear and version B masks it is a "regression of A against B"):
- Structured DSN fuzz, seed 11, 20K cases: head shows the secret where 4a284f9 masks it 325 times, e.g. `x=app::#Zq9SeCr3tVal!@unix(/tmp/s)/app?parseTime=true`. The fix has 0 such cases against 4a284f9 and 0 against head.
- Random-token fuzz, seed 7, 40K cases: head regresses 2 times against 4a284f9, and the fix 0 times against either.

**Fix check.** I swapped in `([^\s/]{1,256})@((?:[a-z][\w-]{0,31})?\(|\/)`. All 71 head tests pass with `--test-force-exit`. The 'a:' test takes 189 ms against its 1 s limit.

**Cost of the fix** (CPU per 256 KB cell, best of 3):

| Text | 4a284f9 | head | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 'a:' | 168 ms | 31 ms | 168 ms |
| 'a:@' | 21 ms | 28 ms | 203 ms |

Other shapes, and plain text, take 7-32 ms at all three heads. Under W28=B this cost is "nit (W28=B: document)" only, and not grounds to give up masking.

**Docs.** README:419 honestly lists "a DSN password with a `:` in it" under misses, so there is no wrong-doc finding. But no documentation exception applies to the blocking classes. Only perf is document-only under W28=B.

**Severity: high.** This is a regression of something previously masked, and a secret shown in clear (in the Data panel; C=c keeps it out of verdicts and GitHub). That matches round 5's standard: the %3d regression was also a narrow shape and also arose between draft rounds, and the '<' regression came from the orchestrator's own suggestion, yet both were rated HIGH.

**Mitigations.** These don't remove the blocker:
- secret-named fields (dsn, database_url, connection_string) are still masked whole;
- the shape needs a neutral field holding a Go DSN whose password contains ':'.

**Also update** when applying the fix:
- the comment at :380 ("never across a ':'");
- the test comment at test:1498 ("the DSN rule never reads past a ':'");
- README:419's misses list.

Then add tests for `root:…:…@tcp(…)` and `root:…:@tcp(…)`.

minor.title: Test gaps: 13 non-equivalent mutants survive. These include the left-out branch where the PR diff lacks the collection, the round-5 `value="it's…"` shape, fieldsBefore taken from the after snapshot, and 4 of round 5's named mutants
minor.evidence:
mutate-f.mjs ran 78 mutants; 17 survive (out-mutate-f.txt). The non-equivalent survivors:
- **leftOut only when omitted.** This drops the `!Object.hasOwn(prDiff.collections, …)` branch. probe-leftout (a) shows that branch is the realistic case: users left out of both S1 and Sn, so the PR diff lacks it entirely. The test covers only `omitted` set.
- **leftOut only for omitted 'after'.** The 'before' side is untested.
- **ATTR_VALUE double-quoted value `"([^"']*)"`.** `<add key="DbPassword" value="it'shunter2Zq"/>`, the exact round-5 shape, is masked in code but not pinned: the test uses the single-quoted mirror.
- **fieldsBefore from `a?.fields`.** Tests diff the base with itself only.
- **cols: others unsorted.**
- **Round-5 'tests to add' that don't kill their mutants:**
  - `spaces31` uses 31 spaces, which `\s{0,31}` also accepts; it needs 32.
  - Upper-case `MYSQL -p…` is untested.
  - A namespaced element `<ns:add key=… value=…>` (ATTR_TAG `[\w:.-]`) is untested.
  - Cleared on 3 rows with the base clearing row 1: the 'merge drops earlier items' mutant keeps row 3, so it stays unshared. The base must clear row 3. Effect: `shared` only, since cleared is amber anyway.
- **Minor:**
  - `\r` in the backslash strip;
  - a row pair with two value fields;
  - the softDelete guard in a pair row;
  - leftOut applied to the null PR-only fold.

Equivalent or near-equivalent survivors:
- percent start only after `%3[ad]` (the strip compensates);
- FLAG `(?=\s)` (KEY_IN_TEXT reads `--x=`);
- DSN network required (`@(` alone isn't a DSN);
- the last secret name in pairOf (digest only).

The author's '19 of 22 killed' didn't include these.

minor.title: A seeded collection the PR's padding pushes into a count-only stub, wiped by UPDATE, is one red 'unverified' that still sorts after every other seeded collection's column-dropped and mass-change flags
minor.evidence:
**probe-stub.** The PR adds collections bigger than users (scaled down with maxCollections S+2; in production that means 1,000 PR collections with more rows), so users (30 rows) is a stub in both PR snapshots. The click sets every email to NULL. The diff entry is `{status:'unknown', truncated:true, omitted:null, countBefore:30, countAfter:30}`.

Users' only flag is a red `unverified`:
- at index 10 of 11 with S=5;
- at index 100 of 101 with S=50.

It comes after each other seeded collection's red column-dropped and mass-change flags. 4a284f9 is the same, so this is not a regression.

The round-5 low's fix covers 'may have left out' (`omitted`, or absent from the PR diff). A cut-short collection the base didn't cut short is the same hiding vector, but it stays in group 2 by design: the test asserts big:unverified after zz:mass-change. Pushing it out of #36's 500-flag list needs roughly 250 other seeded collections, each with its own red flags.
minor.fix: Rank a red base-pane `unverified` whose PR side is cut short where the base's isn't with what loses rows too. Keep only the amber case (cut short in both, no count change) late. Or say in the README order paragraph that this case is ranked late.

minor.title: Over-masking keys: the row-level pair rule masks key fields named value/val/v, so renaming a row's name turns an update into a red delete plus an insert
minor.evidence:
probe-over.mjs (out-over.txt), 4a284f9 against 4ed6449.

O1: pages keyed [id, v], with a row named 'Session expired page'. v becomes {t:'secret'}. The click renames the row to 'Expired page', so v turns plain.
- 4a284f9: 1 update, no flags.
- 4ed6449: 1 insert and 1 delete, with flags [['pages','delete','red']].

O2: options keyed [value] with name 'Password reset': the same thing happens.

O3: renaming key 'session_timeout' to 'idle_timeout' adds a spurious update {field:'value', before:{t:'secret'}, after:'30'}.

O4: ordinary config under secret-looking names is now digests: session_timeout 30, card_layout grid, hash_algorithm bcrypt, and a 'Passport photo' URL.

Ids that the %xx-start and DSN rules mask (`/a%2Fsession=1`, `acct:42@/org`) stay deterministic, so those keyed diffs still match.
minor.fix: Don't apply the row-level pair to the collection's key fields: skip it where `named` includes the field. Note in the README that a row's value fields mask or unmask when its name changes.

minor.title: Deletes hidden behind a cut made only in the PR pane stay at the back: round 6 moved only the left-out collections' 'unverified' forward
minor.evidence:
Two ways a PR can cut a seeded collection short in its own pane, then replace all its seeded rows with as many padding rows so the count doesn't change:
- inflate it past maxRows (probe-flags F, maxRows 100);
- push it into the count-only stubs by adding maxCollections bigger collections (probe-stub, maxCollections 5 standing for 1,000).

Its only flag is then a red 'unverified' at late 2, sorted after every column and mass-change flag:
- F: users is at index 40 of 41 with 10 padded seeded collections, and 400 of 401 with 100, at all three heads;
- probe-stub: index 9 of 10 at both heads.

The left-out case (E) did improve: 40 to 20, and 400 to 200. It now ranks by collection name among the deletes, so PR-made delete and key-lost flags on seeded collections that sort earlier still come first.

README:446 justifies moving left-out collections up because they 'can hide a drop or a wipe'. A cut made only in the PR pane can hide wholesale deletes the same way. None of this is a regression.
minor.fix: In `late`, also rank as 0 an 'unverified' flag on a collection the base pane kept whole (b.truncated false) while the PR pane's is cut short, as leftOut does. Update README:446 and the CHANGELOG to match.
